ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Exclude hemorrhage before treatment

A patient arrives with sudden unilateral weakness and aphasia. The stroke team considers intravenous thrombolysis after establishing timing and other eligibility factors. Which finding on urgent brain imaging would most directly rule out treating this event as an ischemic stroke with alteplase?

  1. Intracranial hemorrhage
  2. No visible early infarct
  3. A remote small lacunar infarct
  4. Age-related cerebral atrophy
  5. Chronic nonspecific white-matter changes
Answer and explanation

Intracranial hemorrhage

Current intracranial bleeding contraindicates ischemic-stroke thrombolysis.

Option explanations

Intracranial hemorrhage: Current intracranial bleeding contraindicates ischemic-stroke thrombolysis.

No visible early infarct: Early ischemia may not yet be visible on noncontrast CT.

A remote small lacunar infarct: A remote lesion requires context but is not equivalent to current hemorrhage.

Age-related cerebral atrophy: Atrophy alone does not establish a bleeding stroke.

Chronic nonspecific white-matter changes: Chronic white-matter changes do not by themselves identify active hemorrhage.
